migrate.title: Move EV Planner 1.x here
migrate.description:
EV Planner 1.x is installed with the household **{title}** ({cars} cars, {chargers} chargers). From version 2.0 EV Planner has a new domain, `ev_household_planner`, because another integration in the Marketplace uses `ev_planner`.

Submit to move everything here: the setup, the cars and chargers, settings, plans, history, learning and photos. The entities keep their entity ids, so dashboards and automations that use them go on working. Actions are now called `ev_household_planner.*`.

The 1.x household is removed afterwards. Delete the folder `custom_components/ev_planner` and restart Home Assistant.

user.title: Add car
user.description: Pick the car's device in Home Assistant and EV Planner fills in its sensors and charge switch (you check them on the next page). You can also start from a car in EV Smart Charging (it is not changed), or from scratch.

data_description.device: Optional. Its charge level, charge limit, plug, charging and location are found for you.

details.title: Car
details.description: Tell EV Planner about the car. Settings such as target, ready by and rules are changed in the panel or with the car's entities.

data_description.name: For example Tesla Model 3.
data_description.battery_capacity: Usable capacity in kWh. Used when the car does not report it itself. With the charging power, it gives the first estimate of the charging speed; after that, the car's own charges decide.

sensors.name: Sensors from the car
sensors.description: Leave empty what the car does not have.

data_description.soc_entity: The car's battery level (%). Without it, you set the level by hand.
data_description.target_entity: The car's own charge limit (%). A number entity is also changed when you change the target in EV Planner.
data_description.capacity_entity: Optional. A sensor with the car's usable battery capacity (kWh). Replaces the number above while it has a value.
data_description.connected_entity: An entity that shows whether the car is plugged in, e.g. a charge cable sensor.
data_description.unplugged_states: Default: off, disconnected, unplugged. For a status sensor, e.g. 3.
data_description.home_entity: Optional. The car's location (a device tracker). EV Planner only acts while the car is at home, or at another place you have added, and finds the car's charger among the chargers there.
data_description.charging_entity: Optional. Shows whether the car is charging (on/charging, or a power above 0). Used to check that charging started.
data_description.power_entity: Optional. The car's own charging power sensor (kW). EV Planner learns the power from it and counts the energy with it.
data_description.refresh_entity: Optional. A button, a script or an entity of the car's integration. When a charger gets a car and it is not known which, EV Planner presses the button, runs the script or updates the entity, so the car reports at once instead of at its next turn. At most twice for one plug-in.

charging.name: Charging at home
charging.description: Where the car charges, and who starts and stops it.

data.control_backup: The other one is the backup

data_description.charge_power: What the car draws when charging at home (kW). A starting point: a car with a charging power sensor is measured instead.
data_description.charger: The charger the car uses. Cars on the same charger share it. Found each time: EV Planner finds the charger from where the car is and which charger got a car. Choose that when the car uses several chargers.
data_description.control: Choose the car, the charger, or neither. A charger is more often there to answer than a car.
data_description.control_entity: Needed when the car starts and stops charging, e.g. switch.model3_charge.
data_description.current_entity: A number that sets the charging current (A), e.g. the car's charging amps or the charger's current limit, or any sensor of an Easee charger (EV Planner then uses Easee's own action). With it, cars on a shared supply share the current; without it they take turns.
data_description.phase_entity: Optional: a switch that sets the charger to three phases (on) or one (off). On the sun, one phase lets the car charge from about 1.4 kW instead of 4.1 kW.
data_description.control_backup: When the first does not answer, the other steps in: the car's own switch when the charger starts and stops charging, the charger's when the car does. What paused the car is also what starts it again.

data_description.calendar_entity: Trips in this calendar set when the car must be ready.
data_description.calendar_keyword: Only events with this word. Write e.g. 90 % in the event to charge to 90 %.

user.title: Add place
user.description: A place with chargers besides your home, a summer house say. It has its own supply, so a car that charges there does not count on the supply at home. Afterwards, choose the place in each charger's settings, and add its solar panels, home battery and heat pump as parts of their own.

data_description.name: For example Summer house.
data_description.zone: The zone in Home Assistant the cars are in when they are here. A car is at this place when its location entity shows this zone.

data.supply_guard: Guard: turn the cars down at once

data_description.supply_limit: The most the house may draw per phase, e.g. 23 A on a 25 A supply, or the circuit the chargers share. 0 turns it off.
data_description.supply_phases: How many phases the supply and the cars charge on.
data_description.supply_meter: Current sensors (A) for the phases, e.g. from a HAN/P1 reader, a Shelly EM or an Equalizer. EV Planner learns what the house draws hour by hour.
data_description.supply_reserve: Without a meter: what the house is expected to draw per phase.
data_description.supply_guard: When the meter shows more than the limit, lower the cars right away (the last in line first) and raise them again after a few minutes. Not a fuse: leave it off if an Equalizer or the charger already balances the load.
data_description.supply_share: When there is not room for all the cars in an hour. In line: the car that must be ready first takes what it needs, the next takes the rest. By need: they share by the kWh each lacks, never less than 6 A each.
data_description.weather_entity: A weather entity with an hourly forecast. EV Planner learns how much more the house draws when it is cold, and counts on the night's temperature.

grid.name: The grid, for charging on the sun
grid.description: With a sensor for the power to and from the grid, a car can charge on what the place would otherwise sell.

data.grid_power_inverted: The grid sensor is negative when the house buys
data.export_price_entity: Sensor with the price you sell at

data_description.grid_power: W or kW, positive when the house buys from the grid and negative when it sends to it (a HAN/P1 reader or the inverter).
data_description.grid_power_inverted: Turn on if your sensor shows it the other way round.
data_description.export_price: What a kWh sent to the grid pays. A kWh of the sun in a car then costs that much in the history, as it was not sold. 0: the sun is counted as free.
data_description.export_price_entity: A sensor with the price per kWh right now. Used before the fixed price.
